en: Dependent on a state that is with-conflict (*saraṇa*) and limited-object (*parittārammaṇa*), a state that is without-conflict (*na-saraṇa*) and not limited-object arises by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on a state that is without-conflict and limited-object, a state that is without-conflict and not limited-object arises by way of root-condition.
[Under] root [condition] there are two; ... pe ... [under] non-disappearance [condition] there are two.

Dependent on a state that is with-conflict (*saraṇa*) and has a sublime object (*mahaggatārammaṇa*), there arises a state that is without-conflict (*na-saraṇa*) and does not have a sublime object, by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on a state that is without-conflict (*araṇa*) and has a sublime object, there arises a state that is without-conflict and does not have a sublime object, by way of root condition.
[Under] root [condition] there are two; ... pe ... [under] non-disappearance condition there are two.

Dependent on a state that is without conflict (*araṇa*) and has an immeasurable object (*appamāṇārammaṇa*), there arises a state that is neither with conflict nor with an immeasurable object by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*). [Under] root [condition], one; ... pe ... [under] non-disappearance [condition], one.
